newsitem.title: USA: Calif. welfare reform measure stalls in Assembly.
newsitem.headline: Calif. welfare reform measure stalls in Assembly.

text.p: A California bill to limit cash payments to welfare recipients has stalled in a state Assembly committee and appears to be dead, state officials said on Friday.
The Assembly rejected a motion by the bill's author, Assemblyman Keith Olberg, to remove the legislation from the Democrat-controlled Human Services Committee. The panel rejected the bill on April 1.
"It's dead for now," Olberg's legislative adviser, Lance Hastings, said after the assemblyman's motion was rejected.
Olberg's Assembly Bill 98 would have limited cash payments to welfare recipients to the amount a person could earn by working a 40-hour week for the minimum wage.
The bill was one of several controversial welfare reform proposals floated earlier this year by state Republicans.

Opponents of Olberg's bill argued that at $5.75 per hour, a minimum wage job does not provide a living wage for a family. The federal poverty level for a family of three is $1,111 per month, compared with $996 provided by a minimum-wage job.
